nodes.summary: Let $d$ denote the normalized Hamming distance on permutations. A group $G$ is sofic if for every finite subset $F \subseteq G$ with $1 \in F$ and every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are an integer $n \ge 1$ and a map $\varphi$ from $F$ to the permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $\varphi(1)$ is the identity, $d(\varphi(gh), \varphi(g)\varphi(h)) < \varepsilon$ for all $g, h \in F$ with $gh \in F$, and…
nodes.title: Sofic groups

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and permutations $\sigma$, $\tau$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Hamming distance $d(\sigma, \tau)$ is the number of points $i < n$ with $\sigma(i) \ne \tau(i)$, divided by $n$, as a real number; for $n = 0$ it is $0$. It is used in the definition of sofic groups [KOU-21.86].
nodes.title: Hamming distance for sofic approximations
